scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Bappiriyan Theyyam originates from the North Malabar region of Kerala, India.
It is a type of Mappila Theyyam, performed by the Vannan community.
The mythological figure Bappiriyan is believed to be a Muslim merchant and ship captain, linked with the Hindu goddess Arya Poonkani.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Bappiriyan Theyyam is performed during temple festivals in North Malabar.
It enacts myths that emphasize Hindu-Islamic religious harmony.
The ritual climbing and shaking of coconut trees is a key ceremonial moment, symbolizing mythological narratives and spiritual themes.
Today it is a living tradition.
